title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: Return an array of the maximum value in every contiguous window of length `k` inside `nums`.
hints: Recomputing the max of each window is correct and costs O(nk).
A deque can store indices in decreasing order of value.
Drop indices that fall out of the window from the front, and drop weaker values from the back before pushing the new index.

approaches.name: Scan each window
approaches.explanation: Take max of nums[i:i+k] for each i.

approaches.name: Monotonic deque
approaches.explanation: Each index is pushed and popped at most once.

editorial: The deque holds candidate indices from front (largest and oldest) to back. Before using the front, pop it if it is left of the window. Before pushing i, pop every back index whose value is less than or equal to nums[i], because those candidates can never win while i is inside the window. Once the window is full, nums[deque[0]] is the answer for that window.

examples.explanation: Each element is its own window.
